# Nexus Flow Dashboard

**About**

This is a modern dashboard application built with React and Vite. The project contains everything you need to run the app locally.

**Getting Started**

1. Clone the repository using the project's Git URL
2. Navigate to the project directory
3. Install dependencies: `npm install`
4. Run the app: `npm run dev`

**Development**

Edit the code in your local development environment. Changes will be reflected immediately thanks to Vite's hot module replacement.

**Building**

To build for production: `npm run build`

**Scripts Available**

- `npm run dev` - Start development server
- `npm run build` - Build for production
- `npm run lint` - Run ESLint
- `npm run lint:fix` - Fix linting issues
- `npm run typecheck` - Type check with TypeScript
- `npm run preview` - Preview production build

The email shall contain an access link and a 6-digit OTP for first-time authentication. Since no password exists initially, the user shall have the option to log in using the OTP or set a new password during first-time login. Acceptance Criteria 1. Trigger: • When a study is published to UAT or LIVE environment (Step 6 of Study Creation), the system automatically triggers invitation emails to all assigned sponsors. • Invitation is sent only once per sponsor per study per environment. • CRO administrator can manually resend invitation if needed. 2. Email Content: • Subject Line: "Invitation to Access [Study Name] - [Environment]" • From: noreply@ sclinnexus .com • Body includes: ◦ Welcome message with sponsor name ◦ Study Name, Protocol Number, Study Phase ◦ Environment (UAT/LIVE) with status ◦ Secure access link (unique, time-limited token) ◦ Instructions that user will set up authentication during first login ◦ Support contact information • No OTP or temporary password is included in the email. 3. Secure Link: • Link Format: https://[workspace-domain]/signin?token=[unique-token] • Token is unique per invitation, hashed, and stored in database. • Token validity: 7 days from generation. • Token identifies the user, study, and environment. • After expiry, link displays error message and user must request new invitation. 4. Email Delivery: • Email sent immediately upon study publication. • If email delivery fails, system retries up to 3 times. • CRO admin is notified of delivery failure after 3 retries. 5. Audit Trail: • All invitation emails are logged in Activity Log with: ◦ Recipient email ◦ Study name ◦ Environment ◦ Timestamp ◦ Delivery status (Sent, Failed, Opened) Default Value • Link expiry: 7 days • Maximum retry attempts: 3 Messages Success: • "Invitation email sent successfully to [Email Address]." • "Invitation resent successfully." Error: • "Failed to send invitation email. Please try again." • "Invitation link has expired. Please request a new invitation." • "Invalid invitation link." Validation: • "Recipient email is required." • "Please enter a valid email address." Mock-up FROM: noreply@ sclinnexus .com TO: sponsor@pfizer.com SUBJECT: Invitation to Access COVID-19 Vaccine Trial - UAT Dear Pfizer Inc., You have been granted access to the COVID-19 Vaccine Trial study in the UAT environment. Study Details: • Study ID: CV-001 • Study Title: COVID-19 Vaccine Trial • Phase: Phase III • Environment: UAT Click the link below to access your workspace: https://cro-workspace.com/signin?token=xyz123 For security reasons, this link will expire in 7 days. During first-time login, you will be guided to set up your authentication method: • Generate a one-time OTP to verify your email • Or set a new password directly If you have any questions, please contact support at support@ sclinnexus.com Thank you, CRO Workspace Team Sign In (Updated with On-Demand OTP & Password Setup) Feature Name Sign In Requirement The system shall provide a secure sign-in page for sponsors. For first-time users (no password exists), the system shall offer two authentication options: (1) generate and verify a 6-digit OTP sent to their registered email, or (2) directly set a new password with confirmation. For returning users (password exists), standard password authentication is used. Additionally, if a user is already logged in and attempts to access the sign-in page, they shall be prompted with email address and password/OTP fields to re-authenticate or switch accounts. Acceptance Criteria 1. Access & Initiation: • Sign-in page is accessible via direct URL or by clicking invitation link. • If accessed via invitation link, email address is pre-filled from token and read-only. • If accessed directly, both email and password fields are editable. • System determines if user has an existing password. 2. Already Logged In Scenario: • If a user who is already logged in attempts to access the sign-in page (e.g., opens new tab, clicks sign-in link), the system shall: ◦ Display the sign-in page with the user's email address pre-filled. ◦ Prompt for authentication based on user's account status: • If password exists: Prompt for Password • If no password exists (first-time): Prompt for OTP with option to set password ◦ User must authenticate to: • Switch to a different account • Re-authenticate for security-sensitive actions ◦ A note is displayed: "You are currently logged in as [Email]. To sign in with a different account, please authenticate." 3. Sign-in Page – First-Time User (No Password Exists): • Display two authentication options: ◦ Option A: Login with OTP ◦ Option B: Set Password Option A: Login with OTP • User clicks "Generate OTP" button. • System generates a 6-digit numeric OTP and sends to registered email address. • User enters the 6-digit OTP received via email. • System validates OTP (validity: 15 minutes, single-use). • Upon successful OTP verification, user is redirected to Set New Password page. • User must set a permanent password to complete login. Option B: Set Password • User clicks "Set Password" option. • System displays password setup form: ◦ New Password (Mandatory) ◦ Confirm New Password (Mandatory) • User enters and confirms new password meeting strength requirements. • System validates and stores password. • User is automatically logged in after successful password setup. 4. Sign-in Page – Returning User (Password Exists): • Display standard sign-in form: ◦ Email Address (Mandatory) ◦ Password (Mandatory) ◦ Remember Me Checkbox ◦ Sign In Button ◦ Forgot Password? Link 5. Sign-in Page – Already Logged In User: • When an already logged-in user accesses the sign-in page: ◦ Email address is pre-filled and read-only (cannot be changed without re-authentication). ◦ If password exists: Display Password field with "Re-authenticate" button. ◦ If no password exists (first-time): Display OTP field with "Generate OTP" and "Set Password" options. ◦ Additional note: "You are currently signed in as [Email]. Please authenticate to switch accounts or continue." ◦ Upon successful authentication, user can: • Stay logged in with current account • Switch to a different account (if available) • Log out and sign in with new credentials 6. Password Requirements: • Minimum 8 characters • At least one uppercase letter (A-Z) • At least one lowercase letter (a-z) • At least one number (0-9) • At least one special character (!@#$%^&*) • Password strength meter displays as user types. 7. OTP Generation & Verification: • OTP is generated on-demand when user selects "Login with OTP". • OTP is 6-digit numeric code. • OTP is sent to the user's registered email address. • OTP validity: 15 minutes from generation. • OTP is single-use only . • User can request a new OTP if expired or not received. • Rate limiting: Maximum 5 OTP requests per hour. 8. Security Measures: • After 5 failed login attempts (password or OTP), account is locked for 15 minutes. • Failed attempts are tracked and logged. • Passwords are hashed using bcrypt before storage. • OTP is hashed before storage. • All password/OTP fields are masked in UI. 9. Login Confirmation Email: • Upon successful login (via either method), send confirmation email to user's registered email address. • Email includes: ◦ Timestamp of login ◦ IP address ◦ Approximate location ◦ Study accessed (if applicable) ◦ Instructions to contact support if unauthorized 10. Session Management: • Upon successful authentication, create secure session. • Session timeout after 30 minutes of inactivity. • Session token stored securely. • Re-authentication does not create a new session unless user chooses to switch accounts. 11. Audit Trail: • All login attempts (success/failure) are logged in Activity Log with: ◦ User email ◦ Timestamp ◦ IP address ◦ User agent ◦ Status (Success/Failure) ◦ Authentication method (OTP/Password) ◦ Scenario (First-time / Returning / Already Logged In) ◦ Failure reason (if applicable) • OTP generation events are also logged. Default Value • Remember Me: Unchecked by default • Session timeout: 30 minutes • Maximum failed attempts: 5 • Account lockout duration: 15 minutes • OTP length: 6 digits • OTP expiry: 15 minutes • Maximum OTP requests per hour: 5 Messages Success: • "Sign in successful. Redirecting to your workspace..." • "OTP sent successfully to [Email Address]." • "Your password has been set successfully. You are now logged in." • "Confirmation email sent to your registered email address." • "Re-authentication successful. You may now switch accounts." Error: • "Invalid email or password. Please try again." • "Invalid or expired OTP. Please request a new OTP." • "Too many failed attempts. Your account is locked for 15 minutes." • "Too many OTP requests. Please try again later." • "Password does not meet the required criteria." • "Password and confirmation do not match." • "Invitation link has expired. Please request a new invitation." Validation: • "Email is required." • "Password is required." • "OTP is required." • "OTP must be 6 digits." • "Password must be at least 8 characters and include uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character." Info (Already Logged In): • "You are currently signed in as [Email]. Please authenticate to switch accounts or continue." Mock-up Choose Study Feature Name Choose Study Requirement The system shall provide a study selection interface for sponsors who have access to multiple studies. Upon successful authentication, the system shall display all accessible studies and allow the sponsor to select which study workspace to enter. The selection can be remembered for future logins. Acceptance Criteria 1. Trigger & Display: • Choose Study window is displayed immediately after successful authentication. • Triggered only when sponsor has access to two or more studies. • If sponsor has access to only one study, this window is skipped and user is redirected directly to that study workspace. 2. Interface Components: • Header: "Choose Study" • Welcome Message: "Welcome back, [Sponsor Name]. You have access to multiple studies. Please select one to continue." • Search Bar: Filter studies by title or protocol number. Real-time filtering. • Study List: Each study displayed as a card or list item. • Remember my choice: Checkbox to save selection as default. • Logout Button: Option to sign out. 3. Study Card/Item Display: Each study card shall display: • Study Title: Full study name • Protocol Number: Study ID/Protocol number • Study Phase: e.g., Phase III, Phase II • Environment: UAT or LIVE with status indicator (Active/Inactive/Locked) ◦ 🟢 Active ◦ 🔴 Inactive ◦ 🟠 Locked • Last Accessed Date: Date and time of last access (if available) • Select Button: Action to enter workspace 4. Search Functionality: • Search bar with placeholder: "Search by study name or protocol number..." • Filters in real-time as user types. • Searches across Study Title and Protocol Number. • Displays message if no matching studies: "No studies match your search criteria." 5. Remember My Choice: • When checkbox is selected and user chooses a study: ◦ Selected study is saved as default for future logins. ◦ On next login, user is automatically redirected to this study workspace (skipping Choose Study window). • User can change default selection by: ◦ Unchecking "Remember my choice" and selecting a different study, or ◦ Using the Study Switcher in workspace header to change context. 6. Study List Behavior : • Studies are sorted by Last Accessed date (most recent first). • If no last accessed data, sort alphabetically by Study Title. • Pagination or scrolling for large lists (show 10 studies per page). 7. Selection Action: • Clicking "Select" navigates to the corresponding study workspace. • Study context is stored in session. • Header in workspace displays current study with Study Switcher dropdown. 8. Empty State: • If no studies are available (should not occur for triggered window), display: ◦ "No studies assigned. Please contact your administrator." ◦ Logout button prominently displayed. 9. Study Switcher in Workspace: • After selecting a study, the workspace header displays a dropdown Study Switcher. • Clicking the switcher shows all accessible studies. • Selecting a different study navigates to that study's workspace. • The "Remember my choice" setting persists across sessions. Default Value • Remember my choice: Unchecked by default • Sort order: Last Accessed date (most recent first) • Page size: 10 studies per page Messages Welcome: • "Welcome back, [Sponsor Name]. You have access to multiple studies. Please select one to continue." • "Showing X of Y studies." Search: • "Search by study name or protocol number..." • "No studies match your search criteria." Empty State: • "No studies assigned. Please contact your administrator." Success: • "Redirecting to [Study Name] workspace..." • "Default study saved successfully." Error: • "Failed to load studies. Please try again." Mock-up Sponsor Menu Feature Name Sponsor Menu Requirement The system shall provide a comprehensive left navigation menu for the Sponsor Workspace, enabling sponsors to access all study-related modules and features. The menu structure shall be role-based, displaying only those modules for which the user has appropriate permissions. Explanation This defines the primary navigation structure for the Sponsor workspace, ensuring users can access all modules based on their permissions. Mandatory fields N/A Interface Messages N/A Business Rules Menu items displayed must be dynamically controlled by the user's assigned role and permissions. The menu structure is as follows: EDC ePRO Survey Dashboard Data Capture Consent Management Consent Builder Consent Review & Approval Quality Management Query Manager Data Verification Manager Site Management Sites Site Personnel Site Role Masters Email Templates Country Locations Activity Log Profile Settings My Profile Change Password Logout Dashboard My Diary Consent Management Consent Builder Consent Review & Approval Quality Management Query Manager Data Verification Manager Site Management Sites Site Personnel Site Role Masters Email Templates Country Locations Activity Log Profile Settings My Profile Change Password Logout Dashboard Take Survey Consent Management Consent Builder Consent Review & Approval Quality Management Query Manager Data Verification Manager Site Management Sites Site Personnel Site Role Masters Email Templates Country Locations Activity Log Profile Settings My Profile Change Password Logout The header shall contain icons/functions for: Maximize/Minimize Left Nav, Choose Sponsor Workspace dropdown, and a Global Search bar. 3. Role-Based Visibility: • Menu items shall be displayed based on user's role and permissions configured in Role & Access Control. • If a user does not have permission to access a module, the menu item shall be hidden. • Sub-menu items shall only be visible if the parent module is accessible. 4. Active State & Navigation: • Current active menu item shall be highlighted to indicate user's current location. • Clicking on a menu item navigates to the corresponding page. • Parent modules with sub-menus shall expand/collapse when clicked. 5. Menu Icons: • Each menu item shall have an associated icon for visual identification. • Icons shall be consistent across the application. 6. Responsive Behavior : • On desktop, menu shall be displayed as a fixed left panel. • On tablet/mobile, menu shall be collapsible into a hamburger icon. 7. Study Switcher Integration: • When multiple studies are available, a Study Switcher dropdown shall appear in the header, not in the left menu. • Switching studies shall reload the workspace while maintaining menu structure. 8. Logout: • Logout option shall be available in Profile Settings or as a separate menu item at the bottom. Masters Email Templates Feature Name Email Templates Requirement The system shall provide email template management capabilities for sponsors to create, edit, and manage study-specific email templates. These templates shall be used for automated communications including site personnel invitations, adverse event triggers, study close-out notifications, and other study-related communications. Templates shall be created during study setup and rolled up with UAT/LIVE database creation. Acceptance Criteria Access & Initiation: • Accessible within Sponsor Workspace under "Masters > Email Templates". • Available only to users with appropriate permissions (Sponsor Admin, Study Manager). • Templates are study-specific and scoped to the current selected study. • Upon study creation (study-specific database creation), this feature's related tables and email templates are created and available for further modifications or usage. 2. Template Creation: • Template Name : Text field (Mandatory, Unique within study) • Template Code : Text field (Mandatory, Unique) – System identifier • Email Category : Dropdown selection (Mandatory) ◦ Site Personnel Invitation ◦ Site Personnel Removal ◦ Site Personnel Status Change (Active/Inactive) ◦ Adverse Event Trigger ◦ Study Close Out ◦ Study Lock Out ◦ Data Entry Reminder ◦ Query Raised ◦ Query Resolved ◦ Consent Request ◦ Consent Approved ◦ Enrollment Target Reached ◦ Site Activation ◦ Site Deactivation ◦ Custom • Subject Line : Text field (Mandatory) – Supports placeholders • Email Body *: Rich Text/HTML Editor (Mandatory) – Supports placeholders • Description : Text area (Optional) – Purpose and usage notes • Status : Dropdown (Active/Inactive) – Default: Active 3. Placeholder/Variable Support: The following placeholders shall be available for use in subject and body: • { StudyName } – Name of the study • { StudyID } – Protocol number/Study ID • { SiteName } – Name of the site • { SiteCode } – Site code • { PersonName } – Recipient's full name • { PersonEmail } – Recipient's email address • { PersonRole } – Role of recipient (PI, Coordinator, etc.) • { InvitationLink } – Unique invitation link • { LoginLink } – Workspace login link • { AdverseEventID } – AE identifier • { AdverseEventDescription } – Brief AE description • {Severity} – AE severity level • { QueryID } – Query identifier • { QueryField } – Field name with query • { QueryDescription } – Query details • { EnrollmentCount } – Current enrollment number • { EnrollmentTarget } – Target enrollment number • { CloseOutDate } – Study close-out date • { LockOutDate } – Study lock-out date • { SupportEmail } – Support contact email • { CurrentDate } – Current date • { CurrentTime } – Current time 4. Template Categories & Default Templates: The system shall pre-create the following default templates for each study during UAT/LIVE database rollup: Site Personnel Templates: • Site Personnel Invite – Sent when site personnel are invited to the study • Site Personnel Removal – Sent when site personnel are removed from the study • Site Personnel Active – Sent when site personnel account is activated • Site Personnel Inactive – Sent when site personnel account is deactivated Adverse Event Templates: • Adverse Event Trigger – Sent when a serious adverse event is reported Study Status Templates: • Study Close Out – Sent when study is closed out • Study Lock Out – Sent when study is locked (no further data entry) Site Management Templates: • Site Activation – Sent when a site is activated • Site Deactivation – Sent when a site is deactivated • Enrollment Target Reached – Sent when a site reaches enrollment target Query Templates: • Query Raised – Sent when a new query is raised on data entry • Query Resolved – Sent when a query is resolved Consent Templates: • Consent Request – Sent when consent is required from participant • Consent Approved – Sent when consent is approved Data Entry Templates: • Data Entry Reminder – Sent as reminder for pending data entry 5. Template Management Functions: • Create: Add new custom templates • Edit: Modify existing templates • Delete: Remove templates (with dependency check) • Duplicate: Copy existing template for quick creation • Preview: Preview rendered email with sample data • Test Send: Send test email to logged-in user for verification • Activate/Inactivate: Toggle template availability 6. Database Rollup Integration: • When a study is published to UAT or LIVE environment, the system shall automatically create the default email templates for that study. • Templates shall be rolled up with the study database and scoped to the specific study. • Templates created in UAT environment shall not automatically copy to LIVE; they must be promoted or recreated. • Template modifications after publication are tracked and versioned. 7. Template Usage & Dependency: • System shall track where each template is used (e.g., triggers, workflows). • If a template is in use, deletion shall be prevented with message: "Cannot delete template. It is in use by active triggers/workflows." • Recommendation: Inactivate instead of delete. 8. Preview & Test Functionality: • Preview button shows rendered email with sample placeholder data. • Test Send sends actual email to logged-in user's email address. • Both features help verify formatting and placeholder replacement. 9. Search & Filter: • Search by Template Name, Template Code, Category • Filter by Status (Active/Inactive) • Filter by Category Default Value • Status: Active for new templates • Default templates pre-created during study UAT/LIVE database rollup • All default templates set to Active status Messages Success: • "Email template '[Template Name]' created successfully." • "Email template '[Template Name]' updated successfully." • "Email template '[Template Name]' deleted successfully." • "Test email sent to [Email Address]." These records shall be used throughout the Sponsor Workspace for site addresses, location selection, and geographical reporting. Country records shall be study-specific and rolled up with UAT/LIVE database creation. Acceptance Criteria 1. Access & Initiation: • Accessible within Sponsor Workspace under "Masters > Country". • Available only to users with appropriate permissions (Sponsor Admin, Study Manager). • Country records are study-specific and scoped to the current selected study. • Upon study creation (study-specific database creation), this feature's related tables and default country records are created and available for further modifications or usage. 2. Country Creation: • Country Name : Text field (Mandatory, Unique within study) – Full name of the country (e.g., "United States", "India", "United Kingdom") • Country Code : Text field (Mandatory, Unique) – Two-letter ISO country code (e.g., "US", "IN", "GB") • Dialing Code : Text field (Optional) – International dialing code (e.g., "+1", "+91", "+44") • Description : Textarea (Optional) – Additional notes about the country • Status : Dropdown (Active/Inactive) – Default: Active 3. View Functionality: • Main list view displays the following columns: ◦ Country Name ◦ Country Code ◦ Dialing Code ◦ Description (truncated if long) ◦ Status with visual indicator (Active/Inactive badge) ◦ Actions : Edit, Delete 4. Default Country Records: The system shall pre-create the following default country records for each study during UAT/LIVE database rollup: • United States (US, +1) • India (IN, +91) • United Kingdom (GB, +44) • Canada (CA, +1) • Australia (AU, +61) • Germany (DE, +49) • France (FR, +33) • Japan (JP, +81) • China (CN, +86) • Brazil (BR, +55) • South Africa (ZA, +27) • Mexico (MX, +52) • Singapore (SG, +65) • United Arab Emirates (AE, +971) • Switzerland (CH, +41) 5. Country Management Functions: • Create : Add new custom country records • Edit : Modify existing country records • Delete : Remove country records (with dependency check) • Activate/Inactivate : Toggle country availability via Status field 6. Database Rollup Integration: • When a study is published to UAT or LIVE environment, the system shall automatically create the default country records for that study. • Country records shall be rolled up with the study database and scoped to the specific study. • Country records created in UAT environment shall not automatically copy to LIVE; they must be promoted or recreated. • Country modifications after publication are tracked and versioned. 7. Dependency & Usage: • System shall track where each country record is used (e.g., Sites, Locations, Site Personnel addresses). • If a country record is in use (associated with sites, locations, or personnel), deletion shall be prevented with message: "Cannot delete country. It is in use by existing records (Sites, Locations, Personnel)." • Recommendation: Inactivate instead of delete. 8. Status Control: • Only "Active" countries are available for selection in: ◦ Site address fields ◦ Location master ◦ Site Personnel address fields • "Inactive" countries are hidden from selection but retained in the system for historical data integrity. • Changing a country to "Inactive" does not affect existing records that reference that country. 9. Search & Filter: • Search by Country Name, Country Code, Dialing Code • Filter by Status (Active/Inactive/All) Default Value • Status : Defaults to "Active" for new countries • All other fields are empty until populated Messages Success: • "Country '[Country Name]' created successfully." • "Country '[Country Name]' updated successfully." • "Country '[Country Name]' deleted successfully." Query Check: • Identify fields with unresolved queries • Prevent verification of fields with open queries 7. Default System Roles: The system shall pre-create the following default roles: A. CRO Administrator: • Full permissions across all modules • Cannot be deleted or edited (system-protected) • Can create and manage other roles B. Data Manager: • View, Create, Edit, Export permissions for: ◦ Dashboard ◦ Data Capture ◦ Query Management ◦ Data Verification ◦ Reports • Limited access to Site Management (View only) • No access to Role & Access Control • Can be deleted or edited C. Data Reviewer: • View and Edit permissions for: ◦ Dashboard ◦ Data Verification ◦ Query Management (View only) • Can be deleted or edited • Export permissions for reports D. Site Monitor: • View and Export permissions for: ◦ Dashboard ◦ Site Management (View only) ◦ Reports • No access to Data Capture, Consent Management, Role & Access Control • Can be deleted or edited 6. Role Management Functions: • Create : Add new custom roles with specific permissions • Edit : Modify existing role details and permissions • Delete : Remove roles (with dependency check) ◦ If role has assigned users, deletion is prevented ◦ System message: "Cannot delete role. It is assigned to [X] users." ◦ Recommendation: Inactivate the role instead of deleting • Duplicate : Copy existing role to create new role with similar permissions • View Permissions : Quick view of all permissions assigned to a role • Activate/Inactivate : Toggle role availability for assignment 7. Permission Inheritance & Validation: • View as Prerequisite : View permission is required for any other permission (Create, Edit, Delete, Export) • If View is unchecked, all other permissions are automatically disabled. • System validation message: "View permission is required before granting Create, Edit, Delete, or Export permissions." • Parent-Child Relationship : Permissions for sub-modules are independent of parent modules. ◦ Example: User can have access to "Consent Review & Approval" without "Consent Builder". 8. Role Assignment: • Roles are assigned to users in "Site Personnel" module during user invitation. • A user can have only one role within a study. • Role changes are tracked in Activity Log. 9. Permission Enforcement: • UI elements (menu items, buttons, tabs) are dynamically shown/hidden based on user's permissions. • API endpoints validate permissions before executing actions. • If a user attempts to access a restricted feature, error message is displayed: "You do not have permission to access this feature." 10. Audit Trail: • All role management actions are logged in Activity Log: ◦ Role created (user, timestamp, role details) ◦ Role updated (user, timestamp, permission changes) ◦ Role deleted (user, timestamp, role details) ◦ Role assigned to user (user, timestamp, role, user) 11. Search & Filter: • Search by Role Name, Description • Filter by Status (Active/Inactive/All) Default Value • Status: Active for new roles • All permissions default to OFF (Unchecked) for new roles • Default system roles pre-created with predefined permissions Messages Success: • "Role '[Role Name]' created successfully." • "Role '[Role Name]' updated successfully." • "Role '[Role Name]' deleted successfully." • "Permissions updated successfully."
